whatIf.title: What-if

get.why: What-if runs a long search in the background, often for hours, on every core of your PC at the lowest priority, so you can keep using the PC. A web page cannot do that, so it needs a small program on your own PC: the runner. It sends nothing out; the search and the page both run on your machine.
get.step1: Unzip the file anywhere, open the WhatIfRunner folder and double-click start-runner.cmd.
get.step2: If Windows shows "Open File - Security Warning" ("The publisher could not be verified"), click Run. If it shows "Windows protected your PC" (SmartScreen) instead, click More info, then Run anyway. The program is not signed, so a warning like this is expected the first time.
get.step3: A black window opens, and your browser opens a tab on http://127.0.0.1:8787/. Leave the black window open while you use the page.
get.step4: On that tab, the What-if button, next to Import/Export, opens the search window. Bring your setup once with Import/Export: that page keeps its own saved setups.
get.linuxHeading: Linux (not tested yet, tell us how it went)
get.linuxStep1: Unzip it: unzip WhatIfRunner.zip. It makes a folder WhatIfRunner.
get.linuxStep2: Install Node.js 24 or newer (your package manager, nodejs.org, or nvm install 24). node --version must print v24 or higher.
get.linuxStep3: In a terminal: cd WhatIfRunner, then node tools/whatif/runner/server.mjs --port 8787
get.linuxStep4: Open http://127.0.0.1:8787/ in your browser and leave the terminal open. Ctrl+C in the terminal stops the runner.
get.linuxReport: Tell us what happened at each step: the exact error, your distribution and your Node version.
